title: Intel’s Earnings Call: Growing Demand, Mounting Challenges
gist: Intel's Q3 2026 showed $16.5B revenue (+21%) with data center and AI up 78% but client computing down 5%. Q4 guidance was cautious ($15-16B, EPS $0.25, 38% gross margin) with PC units falling and an Israel Fab 28 disruption.

insights.claim: Intel reported Q3 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year over year, with adjusted EPS of $0.52 and adjusted gross margin of 44.1%, above guidance.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Headline beat contrasted with a weak outlook.
insights.locator: The company reported revenue of $16.5 billion

insights.claim: Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion while Client Computing and Physical AI fell 5% to $8.1 billion, showing a widening split between segments.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Growth is concentrated in servers; the PC side is the drag.
insights.locator: Data Center and AI revenue climbed 78%

insights.claim: CEO Lip-Bu Tan made expanding Xeon supply an immediate priority.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Server CPU demand outstrips supply; supply additions are the swing factor.

insights.claim: Executives attributed PC weakness to higher memory prices, constrained availability and limited customer budgets, with customers also cutting inventories.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Inventory drawdown adds near-term pressure on CPU purchases.

insights.claim: CFO David Zinsner expects PC unit shipments to decline about 12% in 2026 and roughly 10% in 2027.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: No PC rebound in 2027 per Intel's own outlook.

insights.claim: Intel released the 14A 0.9 process design kit in October, a milestone for prospective foundry customers, but investors still need proof that engagement becomes sustained external revenue with improving economics.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Look for named external 14A customers and foundry loss trajectory.

insights.claim: Intel guided Q4 revenue of $15-16 billion, adjusted EPS of $0.25 and adjusted gross margin of 38%, a sharp step down from Q3.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Margin drop of over 6 points explains the share price reaction.

insights.claim: Disruption at Israel's Fab 28 is expected to reduce quarterly revenue by about $300 million.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: One-time-ish hit but duration is uncertain.

insights.claim: Converting AI infrastructure demand into shipments requires added manufacturing and packaging capacity, which must be balanced against PC weakness and foundry losses to turn revenue growth into durable profit.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Capex discipline versus capacity is the key profitability question.
insights.locator: The call therefore presented a recovery
